rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a material structural template: both memoranda accept the soundness of one part or underlying principle of a bill, object to an added procedural mechanism as unnecessary and ill-suited, explain that existing general procedures provide the preferable solution, and invite Congress to enact a narrower measure. The shared wording is not highly distinctive, but this sustained parallel argumentative and operative sequence is substantially stronger than generic veto-message boilerplate. C22 has a similar accept-some/reject-some structure but concerns a less closely parallel administrative mechanism. C03 likewise rejects a proposed remedy while endorsing a narrower alternative, but its sequence is less closely matched.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I favor this change in the law and would approve the bill if it were limited to this provision.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have approved legislation authorizing similar adjustments by reconveyance of lands to former owners (or their heirs) ... because I am convinced of the soundness of the principle
shared_material.explanation: Both distinguish an acceptable underlying reform from an unacceptable additional provision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: These additional steps appear to be unnecessary and unwarranted since, under the present statute, the rights of property owners ... are fully protected.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: These unnecessary burdens and the attendant criticism can, and should, be avoided.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize the added procedural machinery as unnecessary because a more appropriate established process is available.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I believe more thorough consideration of Section 2 is warranted.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I recommend that the Congress reconsider H.R. 7195 and enact a bill along those lines
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by calling for reconsideration directed toward a narrower version preserving the acceptable portion or principle.
